title.narrative: Cambodia Southeast Asia Disaster Risk Management Project 2

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the disaster and climate resilience of flood-damaged rural roads in Target Areas, improve the capacity of the Government to prepare for and respond to emergencies, and provide immediate and effective response in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The development objective of the Second Southeast Asia Disaster Risk Management Project for Cambodia is to improve the disaster and climate resilience of flood-damaged rural roads in target areas, improve the capacity of the Government to prepare for and respond to emergencies, and provide immediate and effective response in case of an eligible crisis or emergency. The project comprises of four components. The first component, institutional strengthening for disaster resilience in the rural development sector consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthening emergency preparedness and response; and (ii) planning and prioritization of rural resilience investment options in the Tonle Sap region. The second component, resilient rehabilitation and reconstruction of rural roads and bridge consists of following sub-components: (i) civil works for rural roads and bridges; and (ii) strengthening institutional capacity for road safety and climate resilience. The third component, project management s includes the provision of technical and operational assistance to strengthen the institutional, organizational, and technical capacity of Ministry of Rural Development (MRD) to support day-to-day project implementation, including coordination, procurement, financial management, social and environmental risk management, monitoring and evaluation, and reporting. The fourth component, contingent emergency response component includes the provision of immediate and effective response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.

condition.narrative: Annual Work Plans and Budgets Section I.F of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient through MRD shall: (a) prepare,not later than November 30 of each year, an annual work plan and budget (“Annual Work Plans and Budget”) for the Project for thefollowing fiscal year of the Recipient, in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Association, covering the activities andexpenditures proposed for the subsequent year of Project implementation, and the source(s) of financing of such activities andexpenditures; which plan and budget shall be of such scope and detail as the Association shall have reasonably requested, exceptfor the Annual Work Plans and Budget for the first fiscal year of the Recipient which shall be furnished to the Association priorto the commencement of the relevant activities under the Project; and (b) thereafter implement the Project during the relevantfiscal year of the Recipient in accordance with such plan and budget as agreed with the Association.

Contingent Emergency Response Component (“CERC”)Section I.E of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementIn order to ensure theproper implementation of contingent emergency response activities under Part 4 of the Project (“Contingent Emergency ResponsePart”), the Recipient shall ensure that:(a) the CERC Manual is prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to theAssociation, which shall set forth detailed implementation arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part, including: (i)any structures or institutional arrangements for coordinating and implementing the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (ii)specific activities which may be included in the Contingent Emergency Response Part, Eligible Expenditures required therefor(“Emergency Expenditures”), and any procedures for such inclusion; (iii) financial management arrangements for the ContingentEmergency Response Part; (iv) procurement methods and procedures for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (v) documentationrequired for withdrawals of Financing amounts to finance Emergency Expenditures; (vi) a description of the environmental and socialassessment and management arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; and (vii) a template Emergency Action Plan; (b)the Emergency Action Plan is prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to the Association; (c) the Emergency ResponsePart is carried out in accordance with the CERC Manual and the Emergency Action Plan; provided, however, that in the event ofany inconsistency between the provisions of the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan and this Agreement, the provisions of thisAgreement shall prevail; and (d) neither the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan is amended, suspended, abrogated, repealed orwaived without the prior written approval by the Association. 2. The Recipient shall ensure that the structures and arrangementsreferred to in the CERC Manual are maintained throughout the implementation of the Contingent Emergency Response Part, withadequate staff and resources satisfactory to Association. 3. The Recipient shall ensure that: (a) the environmental and socialinstruments required for the Contingent Emergency Response Part are prepared, disclosed and adopted in accordance with the CERCManual and the ESCP, and in form and substance acceptable to the Association; and (b) the Contingent Emergency Response Part iscarried out in accordance with the environmental and social instruments in a manner acceptable to the Association. 4. Theactivities under the Contingency Emergency Response Part shall be undertaken only after an Eligible Crisis or Emergency hasoccurred.

Environmental and Social StandardsSections I.C.1 and I.C.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient, through MRD,shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable tothe Association. Without limitation upon paragraph 1 above, the Recipient, through MRD, shall ensure that the Project isimplemented in accordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. Tothis end, the Recipient, through MRD, shall ensure that: (a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented withdue diligence and efficiency, as provided in the ESCP; (b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing theESCP; (c) policies and procedures are maintained, and qualified and experienced staff in adequate numbers are retained to implementthe ESCP, as provided in the ESCP; and (d) the ESCP, or any provision thereof, is not amended, repealed, suspended or waived,except as the Association shall otherwise agree in writing, as specified in the ESCP, and ensure that the revised ESCP Is disclosedpromptly thereafter.

Institutional Arrangements Section I.A of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient shall maintain, throughout theperiod of implementation of the Project, the Project Management Unit, with a mandate, staffing and resources acceptable to theAssociation, to be responsible for the day-to-day execution of the Project, both at the central and provincial levels.

Project Operations ManualSection I.B of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient shall ensure that the Project iscarried out in accordance with the arrangements and procedures set out in the Project Operations Manual (provided, however, that inthe event of any conflict between the arrangements and procedures set out in the Project Operations Manual and the provisions ofthis Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail) and shall not amend, abrogate or waive any provision of ProjectOperations Manual unless the Association has provided its prior no-objection thereof in writing.

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed in a timely manner

comment.narrative: This indicator assesses the effectiveness of transparency and accountability mechanisms implemented within the project. Fourteen complaints (10 from males and 4 from females) were addressed according to the GRM guidelines and procedures. The complaints included drainage installation/building by residents living in high-risk areas affected by stormwater in the KC2 subproject, the lack of safety signage at KC2, dust pollution and slipperiness after rain on the KC2 bypass road, unstable temporary guardrails at Bridge 3-TK2, and other general issues such as road slipperiness during heavy rain and the absence of nighttime traffic lights for bridges. Some complaints, such as dust control and the installation of traffic signs, were resolved immediately by the contractors.

comment.narrative: As of the September 2025 mission, 31.905 km of rural roads have been completed with climate-resilient features. The end-target value is proposed for revision to 638.29 km under the ongoing restructuring discussion.

title.narrative: Climate change adaptation and disaster risk management principles embedded into the Rural Road Asset Management (RRAM) System

comment.narrative: The functionality of MRD's Rural Road Asset Management (RRAM) System will be expanded to incorporate climate resilience principles in the decision-making process and cover post-disaster data collection and assessment of road damages for recovery investments. Damage data reporting definitions and formats, and methods for validation will be investigated, and recommendations to address these needs will be translated into an actionable roadmap. Intermediate Target 01 indicates that the ToR is developed for the RRAM climate resilience integration.

title.narrative: Post-disaster response and recovery guideline for MRD endorsed

This includes, for example, the development of a response manual and training drills for relevant departments. Intermediate target 01 indicates the completion of EP&R diagnostics and ToRs developed for priority actions through the diagnostics

title.narrative: Vulnerability mapping of MRD infrastructure assets in Target Areas conducted, incorporating latest climate-related disaster information

comment.narrative: Technical analyses of the region's susceptibility to climate-related hazards (primarily heavy rains, rainfall induced landsides and riverine floods) will be conducted. The inventory of MRD assets (rural roads, drainage facilities, irrigation facilities, and other) will also be screened against climate-related hazards to identify vulnerability hotspots. This component will be closely coordinated with the previous ADB-funded Technical Assistance (TA) on climate resilient roads and the on-going CREWS (Climate Resilience and Early Warning Systems) TA , under which an updated national level flood risk assessment will be conducted using CIMA foundation's Food Monitoring Tool (2021) developed for the Southeast Asia Disaster Risk Insurance Facility (SEADRIF). Intermediate Target 01 indicates high-risk areas identified through the first phase flood risk analysis.
